summary: A Q&A-style article in which industry experts explain why small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are vulnerable to cyberattacks and what they can do about it. Topics include affordable tools, AI/ML security, cloud services, employee training, remote work, layered defenses, and breach response. It concludes that vigilance, investment, and expert engagement make SMEs more resilient.
one_line: Experts answer common questions on how SMEs can defend against evolving cyber threats using affordable tools, AI, training, and response planning.
key_facts: SMEs are vulnerable targets because of limited resources and cybersecurity expertise, and their defenses are less mature than those of larger firms.
Jennifer Clarke, a cybersecurity consultant working with SMEs since September 2023, says SMEs often overlook investing in cybersecurity due to smaller budgets.
Jameson Tech, a cybersecurity firm launched in October 2023, offers cost-effective tools for SMEs that use AI and machine learning.

Rajeev Singh published research on SME cybersecurity trends in November 2023 and recommends continuous education, regular software updates, a security culture, and partnering with security service providers.
Maria Gonzalez of SecurePath Solutions advises SMEs to start by assessing their current cybersecurity posture and identifying assets and vulnerabilities.
Oliver Martinez says cloud providers have robust security, but under the shared responsibility model the SME is still responsible for securing its data in the cloud.
Laura Bell says phishing remains the primary entry point for attacks on SMEs and ransomware attacks have become more targeted; she recommends employee training and efficient backup strategies.
NextGen Security introduced an AI-driven security platform for SMEs in January 2024, according to its CTO Peter Kim.
Kristina Voss of CyberSafe Workforce says trained employees can be the first line of defense against cyberattacks.
Mark Turner says firewalls and antivirus software are foundational but not foolproof, and SMEs need multiple layers of defense including physical security and encryption.
Diana Young recommends strong policies, VPNs, endpoint protection, and regular audits to secure remote workforces.
Michael Soh, a cybersecurity attorney, says SMEs need a breach response plan covering legal actions, stakeholder communication, and preventing future breaches.
